resourceProfile.assessment: The complete English and Icelandic source scope, review metadata, glossary, and project concept references were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review checks, typecheck, complete build, route and generated-link checks, and the full test suite passed after the cycle was finalized.

linguisticCritique.summary: A bounded Icelandic pass identified ten remaining trigonometry and unit-translation defects; all ten were corrected.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent Icelandic human review was performed in this cycle; changed IDs remain machine-drafted.

publicationAuthorization.summary: No merge, publication, deployment, or residual-risk authorization was requested or granted for this cycle.

findings.summary: The Icelandic right-triangle formulas retained English side labels.
evidence: The formulas used opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse instead of gagnstæða, aðliggjandi, and undirstúka.
findings.resolution: Localized all three side labels in the formulas.

findings.summary: The inverse-trigonometry formulas retained English side labels.
evidence: The previous expressions contained opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse.
findings.resolution: Localized the side labels while preserving inverse-function notation.

findings.summary: The worked trigonometry example retained English side labels.
evidence: The example formulas began with opposite and adjacent.
findings.resolution: Changed the labels to gagnstæða and aðliggjandi.

findings.summary: The yard conversion retained the English unit name.
evidence: The previous formula was 1 yard = 3 fet = 0,9144 m.
findings.resolution: Changed yard to the Icelandic jarda form.

findings.summary: The square-inch conversion used an unexplained English abbreviation in an otherwise localized section.
evidence: The previous formula began 1 in² while the other length units were written in Icelandic.

findings.summary: The prose and formulas used different conventions for the Icelandic side terms.
evidence: The paragraph already used Icelandic side names while the formulas retained English names.
findings.resolution: Aligned formula terminology with the established Icelandic prose.

findings.summary: The inverse-formula labels were inconsistent with the localized right-triangle explanation.
evidence: The inverse formulas did not reuse the Icelandic side terminology from the preceding explanation.
findings.resolution: Made the inverse formulas consistent with the surrounding Icelandic text.

findings.summary: The worked-example labels were inconsistent with the localized inverse formulas.
evidence: The example retained English labels after the explanatory paragraph had been localized.
findings.resolution: Aligned the example labels with the Icelandic terminology.

findings.summary: The imperial length formulas mixed English and Icelandic unit naming.
evidence: The yard and square-inch formulas did not match the localized inch and foot formulas.
findings.resolution: Normalized the remaining length-unit names in the Icelandic section.

findings.summary: The Icelandic trigonometry section was not internally consistent across prose, formulas, and examples.
evidence: A single worked example mixed English labels with Icelandic explanatory text.
findings.resolution: Applied one consistent Icelandic terminology set throughout the section.
